concepts.title: Congiuntivo presente after opinion, emotion, wish and doubt
concepts.rule: Verbs of opinion, emotion, wish, doubt and impersonal judgements (penso che, sono contento che, voglio che, dubito che, è possibile che) take the subjunctive. Verbs of certainty (so che, è chiaro che, sono sicuro che) take the indicative.
assessment: Chooses the subjunctive after opinion, emotion, wish, fear and doubt verbs
Chooses the indicative after verbs and expressions of certainty
Forms the present subjunctive of regular and common irregular verbs correctly
Produces subjunctive clauses when translating from English, where English shows no difference

lesson.intro: English rarely marks the subjunctive ("I think she **is** right"), so English speakers tend to slip into the indicative. In Italian the main verb decides: if it expresses a **personal view, feeling, wish or uncertainty**, the verb after *che* goes into the **congiuntivo**. If it presents something as **fact or certainty**, use the indicative. In careful and formal Italian, getting this right is one of the clearest markers of a C1 speaker.

rules.title: Triggers: subjunctive after che
rules.text: Opinion: *penso, credo, mi sembra, mi pare, ritengo, immagino che*. Emotion: *sono contento, mi dispiace, ho paura, temo, è strano che*. Wish or will: *voglio, spero, preferisco, desidero che*. Doubt: *dubito, non sono sicuro, non è detto che*. Impersonal judgement: *è possibile, è importante, bisogna, è meglio, è normale che*.

examples.en: I think Marco is right.
I'm sorry you're unwell.

examples.it: È importante che tutti **sappiano** la verità.
examples.en: It's important that everyone knows the truth.

rules.title: Certainty takes the indicative
rules.text: *So che, sono sicuro che, è chiaro / evidente / vero che, dimostra che, vedo che* present a fact, so they take the **indicative**. Overusing the subjunctive here is an error too, often made by advanced learners.

examples.en: I know Marco is right.

examples.it: È evidente che la situazione **è** cambiata.
examples.en: It's obvious the situation has changed.

rules.title: Forms: congiuntivo presente
rules.text: -are verbs: *-i, -i, -i, -iamo, -iate, -ino* (parli). -ere/-ire verbs: *-a, -a, -a, -iamo, -iate, -ano* (prenda, dorma, capisca). The three singular forms are identical, so add the subject pronoun when it isn't clear (*che io / tu / lei vada*). The **noi** form is the same as the indicative (*perdiamo*).

rules.title: Same subject: use di + infinitive
rules.text: When the subject of both verbs is the same, Italian uses *di* + infinitive, not *che* + subjunctive: *Penso **di avere** ragione* (not ~~penso che io abbia~~). Exceptions: *volere, preferire, desiderare* take a bare infinitive (*Voglio partire*).

examples.en: I hope to see you soon.
I hope you can come.

mistakes.wrong: Penso che è vero.
mistakes.why: Opinion verb: needs the subjunctive. *Penso che è* is common in fast speech but marked as sub-standard.

mistakes.wrong: So che abbia ragione.
mistakes.why: *Sapere* states a fact, so it takes the indicative.

mistakes.wrong: Credo che lui stii bene.
mistakes.why: *Stare* and *dare* have irregular stems: *stia, dia*, never *stii, dii*.

mistakes.wrong: Penso che io abbia torto.
mistakes.why: Same subject in both clauses: use *di* + infinitive.

tips: Quick test: can you add 'I'm certain that…' without changing the meaning? If so, use the indicative.
In informal speech you'll hear *penso che è*. Recognise it, but don't write it.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Penso che Marco ___ (avere) ragione.

traps.why: *Penso che* expresses an opinion, so it needs the subjunctive: *abbia*.

exercises.en: I think Marco is right.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Mi sembra che tu ___ (essere) un po' stanco oggi.

traps.why: *Mi sembra che* is an impression or opinion, so it takes the subjunctive: *(tu) sia*.

exercises.en: It seems to me you're a bit tired today.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Sono contenta che voi ___ (venire) alla festa.

traps.why: Emotion (*sono contenta che*) needs the subjunctive: *veniate*.
The voi form keeps the regular stem: *veniate* (compare *vengano* for loro).

exercises.explanation: Emotion + che → congiuntivo. *Venire*: venga, venga, venga, veniamo, **veniate**, vengano.
exercises.en: I'm glad you (all) are coming to the party.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Dubito che loro ___ (sapere) la verità.

traps.why: *Sapere* has an irregular subjunctive stem with a double p: *sappia, sappiano*.

exercises.en: I doubt they know the truth.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Temo che Giulia non ___ (stare) bene.
exercises.en: I'm afraid Giulia isn't well.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: È possibile che il treno ___ (fare) ritardo.

traps.why: *È possibile che* is an impersonal judgement of possibility, so it takes the subjunctive.

exercises.en: The train may be late.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Credo che i ragazzi ___ (dovere) studiare di più.

traps.why: *Devano* is non-standard. The standard form is *debbano*.

exercises.en: I think the boys need to study more.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Spero che tu ___ (potere) venire sabato.
exercises.en: I hope you can come on Saturday.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Non sono sicuro che lei ___ (capire) il problema.

traps.why: *Non sono sicuro* expresses uncertainty, so it needs the subjunctive. Note that *sono sicuro che* (certainty) takes the indicative.

exercises.en: I'm not sure she understands the problem.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Ho paura che noi ___ (perdere) il treno.

traps.why: That's the voi form. Here the subject is noi: *perdiamo*.
The main verb is present (*ho paura*), so use the present subjunctive, not the imperfect.

exercises.explanation: Trick question: the **noi** form of the present subjunctive is identical to the indicative: *perdiamo*.
exercises.en: I'm afraid we'll miss the train.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Immagino che voi ___ (essere) stanchi dopo il viaggio.

traps.why: *Immagino che* is a supposition, so it takes the subjunctive: *siate*.

exercises.en: I imagine you're tired after the journey.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: So che Marco ___ (avere) ragione.
exercises.en: I know Marco is right.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: È evidente che la situazione ___ (essere) cambiata.

traps.why: *È evidente che* presents a fact: indicative *è (cambiata)*.

exercises.explanation: Impersonal expressions of **certainty** (è evidente / chiaro / vero che) → indicativo.
exercises.en: It's obvious the situation has changed.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Voglio che tu mi ___ la verità.

traps.why: *Dicessi* is imperfect subjunctive, used after a past or conditional main verb (*Volevo / Vorrei che tu dicessi*). Here *voglio* is present.
Future indicative isn't possible after *volere che*.

exercises.en: I want you to tell me the truth.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: I think she is right.

traps.why: 'To be right' is *avere ragione* in Italian, not *essere*.

exercises.en: I think she is right.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: I'm glad you're here.
answers: (Sono contento|Sono contenta|Sono felice|Mi fa piacere) che [tu] sia qui
(Sono contento|Sono contenta|Sono felice|Mi fa piacere) che [tu] sia qua

traps.why: Use the informal singular, *tu*, and the subjunctive: *sia*.

exercises.en: I'm glad you're here.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence starting with 'Penso che…'.
exercises.prompt: Paolo arriva stasera.

traps.why: *Penso che Paolo arriverà stasera* is also used, because the future can replace the subjunctive for future events. The present subjunctive *arrivi* is the target form here.

exercises.en: I think Paolo is arriving tonight.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: It's strange that nobody is answering.
answers: È strano che non risponda nessuno
È strano che nessuno stia rispondendo

traps.why: The progressive also needs the subjunctive: *stia rispondendo*.

exercises.en: It's strange that nobody is answering.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: I hope you (all) enjoy yourselves at the party.
answers: Spero che vi divertiate alla festa
exercises.explanation: The reflexive pronoun *vi* goes before the conjugated verb: *che vi divertiate*.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite using 'di' + infinitive where the subject is the same.
exercises.prompt: Penso che io abbia sbagliato.
exercises.explanation: Same subject → *penso di* + (past) infinitive: *di aver(e) sbagliato*.

concepts.title: Congiuntivo passato
concepts.rule: When the main verb is in the present (penso, spero, mi dispiace che…) and the action in the che-clause happened before, use the congiuntivo passato: present subjunctive of avere/essere + past participle (abbia finito, sia partita). Certainty still takes the indicative (so che è partito).
assessment: Forms the congiuntivo passato with the correct auxiliary (abbia / sia) and participle agreement
Chooses congiuntivo passato for past actions and congiuntivo presente for present or future ones after a present main verb
Keeps the indicative passato prossimo after verbs of certainty
Uses di + past infinitive (di aver fatto, di essere arrivato) when both clauses share the subject

lesson.intro: English uses a simple past after 'I think' ("I think she **left**"), so learners reach for the passato prossimo: ~~penso che è partita~~. Italian keeps the subjunctive trigger and simply moves it into the past: *penso che **sia partita***. The good news is that if you know the present subjunctive of *avere* and *essere*, you already know this tense. The traps are the auxiliary and the agreement.

rules.title: Form: abbia / sia + past participle
rules.text: Take the auxiliary the verb normally uses in the passato prossimo and put it into the present subjunctive. With *essere*, the participle agrees with the subject, exactly as in the passato prossimo.

rules.title: When: the action came before the main verb
rules.text: With a main verb in the present (or future), choose by time: same time or later → congiuntivo **presente**; earlier → congiuntivo **passato**. Time words like *ieri, già, la settimana scorsa* are your signal.

examples.en: I think Luca is leaving tomorrow.
I think Luca left yesterday.
I hope you slept well.

rules.title: Agreement: essere verbs, reflexives and lo / la / li / le
rules.text: Essere verbs and reflexives agree with the subject (*che Giulia sia venut**a***, *che si siano divertit**i***). With *avere*, the participle agrees with a preceding direct-object pronoun *lo, la, li, le* (*non credo che le abbia lett**e***).

examples.it: Mi dispiace che Anna non si sia sentita bene.
examples.en: I'm sorry Anna didn't feel well.

examples.it: Le chiavi? È possibile che le abbia prese Marco.
examples.en: The keys? Marco may have taken them.

rules.title: Certainty stays indicative
rules.text: *So che, è vero che, sono sicuro che, ho saputo che* report facts, so they take the indicative passato prossimo: *So che **è partito***. Don't over-correct.

examples.it: Sono sicura che ha detto la verità.
examples.en: I'm sure he told the truth.

examples.it: Non sono sicura che abbia detto la verità.
examples.en: I'm not sure he told the truth.

rules.title: Same subject: di + past infinitive
rules.text: If the subject of both clauses is the same, drop *che* and use *di* + past infinitive: *aver(e)* / *essere* + participle. *Credo di aver capito* (not ~~credo che io abbia capito~~). With *essere*, the participle still agrees: *Credo di essere arrivata prima di tutti.*

examples.en: I think I took the wrong road.
We're glad we came.

mistakes.wrong: Penso che Marco è partito ieri.
mistakes.right: Penso che Marco sia partito ieri.
mistakes.why: Opinion verb + past action: congiuntivo passato, not passato prossimo.

mistakes.wrong: Credo che abbia andato a Roma.
mistakes.right: Credo che sia andato a Roma.
mistakes.why: *Andare* takes *essere* in all compound tenses, subjunctive included.

mistakes.wrong: Mi dispiace che Giulia non sia venuto.
mistakes.right: Mi dispiace che Giulia non sia venuta.
mistakes.why: With *essere*, the participle agrees with the subject.

mistakes.wrong: Penso che Luca sia partito domani.
mistakes.why: A future action after a present main verb takes the congiuntivo presente (or the future indicative).

mistakes.wrong: Credo che io abbia capito.
mistakes.why: Same subject: *di* + past infinitive.

tips: Build it in two steps: first the passato prossimo (*è partita*), then swap the auxiliary into the subjunctive (*sia partita*). The participle never changes.
Look for a time marker: *ieri, già, ancora, la settimana scorsa, mai* usually mean congiuntivo passato.
*Non credo che sia mai stato in Giappone*: *mai* and *già* sit between the auxiliary and the participle, as in the passato prossimo.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Penso che Marco ___ (finire) il lavoro ieri sera.

traps.why: *Penso che* still needs the subjunctive in the past: *abbia finito*, not the passato prossimo *ha finito*.
*Ieri sera* places the action in the past, so use the congiuntivo passato: *abbia finito*.

exercises.en: I think Marco finished the work last night.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Mi dispiace che Giulia non ___ (venire) alla festa ieri.

traps.why: With *essere* the participle agrees with Giulia: *venuta*.

exercises.explanation: Emotion + past action → *sia* + participle agreeing with Giulia: **sia venuta**.
exercises.en: I'm sorry Giulia didn't come to the party yesterday.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Credo che i ragazzi ___ (uscire) mezz'ora fa.

traps.why: *Mezz'ora fa* is in the past: congiuntivo passato.

exercises.en: I think the boys went out half an hour ago.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets. Watch the pronoun.
exercises.prompt: Non trovo più le chiavi: è possibile che qualcuno le ___ (prendere) per sbaglio.

traps.why: The direct-object pronoun *le* comes before *avere*, so the participle agrees: *le abbia prese*.

exercises.explanation: Possibility + past → *abbia* + participle. *Le* (the keys, fem. pl.) before *avere* → **prese**.
exercises.en: I can't find my keys: someone may have taken them by mistake.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: So che Paolo ___ (partire) stamattina presto.

traps.why: *So che* states a fact: indicative *è partito*.

exercises.explanation: Certainty (*so che*) → indicative passato prossimo: **è partito**.
exercises.en: I know Paolo left early this morning.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Mi sembra strano che Laura non si ___ (ricordare) del tuo compleanno.

traps.why: *Mi sembra strano che* → subjunctive: *si sia ricordata*.

exercises.en: It seems strange to me that Laura didn't remember your birthday.

exercises.instruction: Present or past subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Penso che domani Giulio ___ (arrivare) tardi.

traps.why: *Domani* is in the future. The congiuntivo passato is only for earlier actions: *arrivi*.
*Arriverà* is also used for a future action after *penso che*. The present subjunctive *arrivi* is the target form.

exercises.explanation: Future action after a present main verb → congiuntivo **presente**, not passato.
exercises.en: I think Giulio will arrive late tomorrow.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Sono contenta che tu ___ l'esame!

optionWhy.0: Emotion (*sono contenta che*) needs the subjunctive.
optionWhy.2: *Superassi* is the imperfect subjunctive, for a past or conditional main verb. *Sono contenta* is present.
optionWhy.3: *Avessi superato* follows a past main verb (*Ero contenta che…*).

traps.why: The main verb is present, so use the congiuntivo passato: *abbia superato*.

exercises.explanation: Present main verb + past action → **abbia superato**.
exercises.en: I'm glad you passed the exam!

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Dubito che Luca ___ ieri sera: aveva la febbre.

traps.why: The action is in the past.

exercises.explanation: Doubt + past action, essere verb → **sia uscito**.
exercises.en: I doubt Luca went out last night: he had a temperature.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Non è detto che il ladro ___ dalla finestra: le impronte sono sulla porta.

optionWhy.1: *Non è detto che* ('it doesn't follow that') expresses doubt: subjunctive.
optionWhy.3: The escape is already over: congiuntivo passato.

exercises.explanation: *Non è detto che* + past action → **sia fuggito**.
exercises.en: It doesn't follow that the thief escaped through the window: the fingerprints are on the door.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence starting with 'Penso che…'.
exercises.prompt: Anna ha perso il treno.
answers: Penso che Anna abbia perso il treno

traps.why: The action is already past: keep it past with *abbia perso*.

exercises.explanation: Passato prossimo → congiuntivo passato: swap *ha* for **abbia**.
exercises.en: I think Anna missed the train.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence starting with 'Non credo che…'.
exercises.prompt: Sono arrivati in ritardo.
answers: Non credo che siano arrivati in ritardo
exercises.en: I don't think they arrived late.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: I hope you had a good trip.
answers: Spero che [tu] abbia fatto (un buon viaggio|buon viaggio)

traps.why: Italian says *fare (un) buon viaggio*, not *avere un buon viaggio*.

exercises.explanation: Hope + past action → *abbia fatto*. Collocation: *fare buon viaggio*.
exercises.en: I hope you had a good trip.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: It's strange that she hasn't called yet.
answers: È strano che [lei] non abbia ancora (chiamato|telefonato)

traps.why: *È strano che* → subjunctive: *non abbia ancora chiamato*.
'Hasn't called' is a completed (non-)event: congiuntivo passato.

exercises.explanation: Judgement + past → *abbia chiamato*. *Ancora* goes between auxiliary and participle.
exercises.en: It's strange that she hasn't called yet.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: I think I made a mistake.

traps.why: Same subject (I think / I made): use *di* + past infinitive, not *che*.
The mistake is in the past: past infinitive *di aver fatto / di aver sbagliato*.

exercises.explanation: Same subject → *penso di* + past infinitive: **di aver sbagliato**.
exercises.en: I think I made a mistake.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: I'm sorry you didn't sleep well.
answers: Mi dispiace che tu non abbia dormito bene
exercises.explanation: *Non* comes before the auxiliary; *bene* follows the participle.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian.
exercises.prompt: A friend tells you Marco didn't come to the party. React, starting with 'Mi stupisce che…' (it surprises me that…).
answers: Mi stupisce che [Marco] non sia venuto [alla festa]

traps.why: Surprise is an emotion: *non sia venuto*.

exercises.en: It surprises me that Marco didn't come (to the party).

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Spero che voi ___ (divertirsi) alla festa di sabato scorso.
exercises.explanation: Reflexive → *essere*, voi → **vi siate divertiti** (*divertite* for an all-female group).
exercises.en: I hope you (all) had fun at the party last Saturday.

concepts.title: Congiuntivo imperfetto e trapassato
concepts.rule: After a main verb in a past tense or the conditional (pensavo, volevo, vorrei, sarebbe meglio che…), use the congiuntivo imperfetto for actions at the same time or later and the congiuntivo trapassato (avessi / fossi + participle) for earlier ones. Come se always takes the imperfetto or trapassato.
assessment: Forms the congiuntivo imperfetto, including essere, dare, stare, fare, dire, bere
Uses imperfetto or trapassato after a past main verb, depending on whether the action is simultaneous or earlier
Uses the imperfetto after a conditional main verb (vorrei che, preferirei che, sarebbe meglio che)
Uses come se + imperfetto / trapassato
Keeps the indicative after past verbs of certainty (sapevo che, era chiaro che)

lesson.intro: English happens to help here: "I wish you **were** here", "as if he **knew**". Italian needs this past subjunctive far more often, though: every time the main verb is in the past or the conditional. ~~Vorrei che tu vieni~~ and ~~pensavo che sia~~ are the two classic learner errors. The forms are very regular. Learn *fossi, dessi, stessi, facessi, dicessi* and the rest follows.

rules.title: Form: congiuntivo imperfetto
rules.text: Take the infinitive stem and its vowel, then add *-ssi, -ssi, -sse, -ssimo, -ste, -ssero*. Almost every verb is regular. *Fare, dire, bere, tradurre* use their long stems (*facevo* → *facessi*).

rules.title: Form: congiuntivo trapassato
rules.text: Imperfect subjunctive of *avere* / *essere* + past participle: *avessi capito, fosse partita, si fossero conosciuti*. Same auxiliary and agreement rules as the passato prossimo.

examples.en: I thought you had already eaten.
We thought they had left.

rules.title: After a past main verb
rules.text: Main verb in the past (*pensavo, ho creduto, temevo, era importante*): same time → **imperfetto**; earlier → **trapassato**. For a later action, Italian normally uses the condizionale passato (*pensavo che sarebbe venuto*), which is covered in the sequence-of-tenses unit.

examples.en: I thought Marta was at home.
I thought Marta had already gone out.

rules.title: After a conditional main verb
rules.text: *Vorrei, preferirei, mi piacerebbe, sarebbe meglio / bello / ora che* are followed by the **imperfetto**, even when the action is in the present or future.

examples.en: I'd like you to come with me.
It would be better if we left right away.

rules.title: Come se: always imperfetto or trapassato
rules.text: *Come se* ('as if') takes the imperfetto (same time) or trapassato (earlier), whatever the tense of the main verb. Never the indicative, never the present subjunctive.

examples.en: He talks as if he knew everything.

examples.it: Si comportava come se niente **fosse successo**.
examples.en: She was behaving as if nothing had happened.

mistakes.wrong: Vorrei che tu vieni con me.
mistakes.right: Vorrei che tu venissi con me.
mistakes.why: Conditional main verb → congiuntivo imperfetto.

mistakes.wrong: Pensavo che Marco sia a casa.
mistakes.right: Pensavo che Marco fosse a casa.
mistakes.why: Past main verb → imperfetto, not presente (concordanza dei tempi).

mistakes.wrong: Volevo che tu stassi zitto.
mistakes.why: *Stare* and *dare* keep their -e- stem: *stessi, dessi*.

mistakes.wrong: Fa come se è il capo.
mistakes.right: Fa come se fosse il capo.
mistakes.why: *Come se* always takes the subjunctive imperfetto or trapassato.

mistakes.wrong: Sapevo che fosse vero.
mistakes.why: *Sapere* states a fact, in the past too: indicative.

tips: Trick for the forms: take the *voi* passato remoto or the infinitive minus *-re*: *parla-* → *parlassi*, *fa(ce)-* → *facessi*.
The *voi* form is the odd one out: *parlaste, foste*, not ~~parlassete~~.
If the main verb ends in *-ei / -ebbe* (conditional), reach for the imperfetto straight away.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Pensavo che tu ___ (essere) a casa.

traps.why: *Pensare che* → subjunctive, even in the past: *fossi*.
The main verb is past (*pensavo*), so the subjunctive moves to the imperfetto: *fossi*.

exercises.explanation: Past main verb, same time → congiuntivo imperfetto: **fossi**.
exercises.en: I thought you were at home.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Vorrei che voi ___ (parlare) più piano.

traps.why: *Vorrei* is conditional, so it takes the imperfetto: *parlaste*.

exercises.en: I'd like you (all) to speak more quietly.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Era importante che tutti ___ (sapere) la verità.
exercises.en: It was important for everyone to know the truth.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Mia madre voleva che io ___ (fare) medicina.
exercises.en: My mother wanted me to study medicine.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Sarebbe meglio che tu ___ (stare) zitto.
exercises.en: It would be better if you kept quiet.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Parla come se ___ (sapere) tutto lui.

traps.why: *Come se* never takes the present subjunctive, even after a present main verb: *sapesse*.

exercises.en: He talks as if he knew everything.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Quando sono arrivata alla stazione, credevo che il treno ___ (partire) da un pezzo.

traps.why: The train leaving comes before *credevo*: trapassato *fosse partito*.
Past main verb → trapassato, not congiuntivo passato.

exercises.explanation: Past main verb + earlier action → trapassato: **fosse partito**.
exercises.en: When I got to the station, I thought the train had left long before.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Sapevo che Marta ___ (avere) un fratello gemello.

traps.why: *Sapevo che* states a known fact: indicative *aveva*.

exercises.explanation: Certainty in the past (*sapevo che*) → indicative imperfetto: **aveva**.
exercises.en: I knew Marta had a twin brother.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Mi ha salutato freddamente, come se noi ___ (litigare) il giorno prima.

traps.why: The quarrel would have happened *before* the greeting: trapassato *avessimo litigato*.

exercises.en: He greeted me coldly, as if we had argued the day before.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Se n'è andato senza salutare, come se ___ (offendersi) per qualcosa.

traps.why: *Come se* takes only imperfetto or trapassato: *si fosse offeso*.
Being offended comes before leaving: trapassato.

exercises.explanation: *Come se* + earlier action, reflexive → **si fosse offeso**.
exercises.en: He left without saying goodbye, as if he'd taken offence at something.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Vorrei che mi ___ un favore.

optionWhy.1: *Vorrei* is conditional: it takes the imperfetto, not the presente.
optionWhy.3: The favour is still to come, not before the wish: imperfetto.

exercises.en: I'd like you to do me a favour.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Bisognava che qualcuno ___ la polizia, ma nessuno l'ha fatto.

optionWhy.2: Past main verb → not the congiuntivo passato.

exercises.en: Someone needed to call the police, but nobody did.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence into the past, starting with 'Pensavo che…'.
exercises.prompt: Penso che Giulia abbia ragione.
exercises.explanation: Presente → imperfetto when the main verb goes into the past.
exercises.en: I thought Giulia was right.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence into the past, starting with 'Credevo che…'.
exercises.prompt: Credo che abbiano già cenato.

traps.why: Congiuntivo passato → trapassato after a past main verb: *avessero cenato*.
Dinner came before: trapassato, not imperfetto.

exercises.en: I thought they had already had dinner.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: I'd like you to come with me.
exercises.en: I'd like you to come with me.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: He talks as if he were the boss.
answers: Parla come se [lui] fosse il capo
Parla come se il capo fosse lui

traps.why: *Come se* never takes the present subjunctive: *fosse*.

exercises.en: He talks as if he were the boss.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: I didn't think they had understood.

traps.why: 'Had understood' is earlier than the thinking: trapassato.

exercises.explanation: Past main verb + earlier action → **avessero capito**.
exercises.en: I didn't think they had understood.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: She was behaving as if nothing had happened.
answers: Si comportava come se niente fosse successo
exercises.explanation: *Come se* + trapassato: *fosse successo*. *Niente* as subject goes first.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian.
exercises.prompt: A colleague asks what your boss wanted. Say that she wanted you to finish the report by Friday.
answers: Voleva che [io] finissi (il rapporto|la relazione|il report) entro venerdì

traps.why: Different subjects (she wanted / I finish): *voleva che io finissi*.

exercises.en: She wanted me to finish the report by Friday.

concepts.title: Conjunctions that need the subjunctive (benché, affinché, prima che…)
concepts.rule: Benché, sebbene, nonostante, affinché, perché (= so that), prima che, a meno che (non), purché, a condizione che and senza che always take the subjunctive. With the same subject, use prima di / senza / per + infinitive instead; anche se, perché (= because) and dopo che take the indicative.
assessment: Uses the subjunctive after concessive, final, conditional and temporal conjunctions
Distinguishes prima che / senza che (different subject) from prima di / senza + infinitive (same subject)
Distinguishes perché + subjunctive (purpose) from perché + indicative (cause)
Keeps the indicative after anche se and dopo che
Applies the sequence of tenses inside these clauses (benché fosse, senza che nessuno se ne accorgesse)

lesson.intro: With conjunctions, the subjunctive isn't about opinion at all: certain words simply demand it. English gives no signal ("although it **is** late"), so you have to know the list. The pairs that trip people up are *anche se* vs *benché* (same meaning, different mood) and *prima che* vs *prima di*.

rules.title: Concession: benché, sebbene, nonostante, malgrado
rules.text: All mean 'although' and all take the subjunctive. *Anche se* ('even though / even if') means much the same but takes the **indicative**. It's the commonest trap.

examples.it: Benché **sia** tardi, il bar è ancora aperto.
examples.en: Although it's late, the bar is still open.

examples.it: Anche se **è** tardi, il bar è ancora aperto.
examples.en: Even though it's late, the bar is still open.

examples.it: Sebbene **avesse** studiato, non ha passato l'esame.
examples.en: Although he had studied, he didn't pass the exam.

rules.title: Purpose: affinché, perché (= so that)
rules.text: *Affinché* and *perché* meaning 'so that' take the subjunctive. *Perché* meaning 'because' takes the indicative, so the mood tells you which meaning you've got. With the same subject, use *per* + infinitive.

examples.it: Te lo ripeto perché tu lo **capisca**.
examples.en: I'm repeating it so that you understand.

examples.it: Te lo ripeto perché non l'**hai capito**.
examples.en: I'm repeating it because you didn't understand.
I'm studying (in order) to pass the exam.

rules.title: Time: prima che vs prima di; dopo che
rules.text: *Prima che* + subjunctive when the subjects differ; *prima di* + infinitive when they're the same. *Dopo che* refers to something that has really happened, so it takes the **indicative**.

rules.title: Condition: purché, a condizione che, a patto che, a meno che (non)
rules.text: 'Provided that' and 'unless' take the subjunctive. After *a meno che* Italians usually add a *non* that is not negative (*a meno che non piova* = unless it rains). It's optional, and it doesn't flip the meaning.

examples.it: Ti presto la macchina purché tu me la **riporti** stasera.
examples.en: I'll lend you the car as long as you bring it back tonight.
I'll come, unless it rains.

rules.title: Senza che vs senza + infinitive
rules.text: *Senza che* + subjunctive when the subjects differ; *senza* + infinitive when they're the same. Never ~~senza di~~ before a verb.

examples.it: È uscito senza che nessuno lo **vedesse**.
examples.en: He went out without anyone seeing him.
He went out without being seen.

mistakes.wrong: Benché è tardi, esco.
mistakes.why: *Benché* always takes the subjunctive.

mistakes.wrong: Anche se sia tardi, esco.
mistakes.why: *Anche se* takes the indicative. Don't over-apply the rule.

mistakes.wrong: Mi lavo le mani prima che io mangi.
mistakes.right: Mi lavo le mani prima di mangiare.
mistakes.why: Same subject: *prima di* + infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: Ti presto il libro purché me lo ridai.
mistakes.right: Ti presto il libro purché tu me lo ridia.
mistakes.why: *Purché* → subjunctive: *ridia*.

mistakes.wrong: Sono partito senza che dire niente.
mistakes.why: Same subject: *senza* + infinitive.

tips: Memorise in pairs: *benché* ↔ *anche se*, *prima che* ↔ *prima di*, *senza che* ↔ *senza*, *affinché* ↔ *per*.
If you're unsure, *anche se* + indicative is always a safe way to say 'although' in speech.
*Nonostante* can also be a preposition: *nonostante la pioggia* (despite the rain). No verb, no subjunctive.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Benché ___ (essere) stanca, Laura continua a lavorare.
exercises.en: Although she's tired, Laura keeps working.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Ti spiego tutto affinché tu ___ (capire).
exercises.en: I'll explain everything so that you understand.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Ti presto la macchina purché tu me la ___ (restituire) entro domenica.

traps.why: No future after *purché*: use the present subjunctive.

exercises.en: I'll lend you the car provided you give it back by Sunday.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Torniamo a casa prima che ___ (cominciare) a piovere.
exercises.en: Let's go home before it starts to rain.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Anche se ___ (essere) tardi, ti chiamo lo stesso.

traps.why: *Anche se* takes the indicative. *Benché* would take *sia*.

exercises.en: Even though it's late, I'll call you anyway.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Abbiamo cenato dopo che i bambini ___ (andare) a letto.

traps.why: *Dopo che* refers to something that really happened: indicative. Don't copy *prima che*.

exercises.en: We had dinner after the children had gone to bed.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Stasera resto a casa, a meno che Giulia non mi ___ (chiamare).

traps.why: *A meno che* → subjunctive: *chiami*. The *non* isn't a negation.

exercises.explanation: *A meno che (non)* + congiuntivo: **chiami**. Meaning: unless Giulia calls me.
exercises.en: I'm staying in tonight, unless Giulia calls me.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Sono uscito senza che nessuno mi ___ (vedere).

traps.why: The main verb is past (*sono uscito*): imperfetto *vedesse*.

exercises.en: I went out without anyone seeing me.

exercises.instruction: Choose the conjunction that fits.
exercises.prompt: Te lo dico ___ tu sappia come stanno le cose.

optionWhy.1: *Anche se* takes the indicative and means 'even though'. It doesn't fit with *sappia*.
optionWhy.3: *Finché* ('until / as long as') doesn't fit the meaning.

exercises.en: I'm telling you so that you know how things stand.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct word.
exercises.prompt: Telefonami prima ___ partire.

optionWhy.0: *Prima che* is followed by a conjugated subjunctive, not an infinitive.

exercises.explanation: Same subject (you call / you leave) → **prima di** + infinitive.
exercises.en: Call me before you leave.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct option.
exercises.prompt: Se n'è andata ___ salutare nessuno.

optionWhy.1: *Senza che* needs a conjugated subjunctive and a different subject.
optionWhy.2: *Senza di* is only used before pronouns (*senza di te*), never before a verb.

exercises.en: She left without saying goodbye to anyone.

exercises.instruction: Choose the conjunction that fits.
exercises.prompt: Ho accettato il lavoro, ___ lo stipendio fosse basso.

optionWhy.1: *Anche se* would need the indicative: *anche se lo stipendio era basso*.
optionWhy.2: *Perché* + subjunctive means 'so that', which makes no sense here.
optionWhy.3: *Dato che* (since) takes the indicative and gives the wrong meaning.

exercises.explanation: *Fosse* signals a subjunctive conjunction, and the meaning is concessive: **sebbene**.
exercises.en: I accepted the job, although the salary was low.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite using 'prima di' + infinitive (the subject is the same).
exercises.prompt: Mi lavo le mani prima che io mangi.
answers: Mi lavo le mani prima di mangiare
exercises.en: I wash my hands before eating.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence replacing 'Anche se' with 'Sebbene'.
exercises.prompt: Anche se ha studiato molto, non ha passato l'esame.
answers: Sebbene abbia studiato molto non ha passato l'esame
Non ha passato l'esame sebbene abbia studiato molto

match: Sebbene ha studiato molto non ha passato l'esame
Non ha passato l'esame sebbene ha studiato molto

exercises.en: Although he studied a lot, he didn't pass the exam.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: I'll lend you the book as long as you give it back to me.
answers: Ti presto il libro (purché|a patto che|a condizione che) [tu] me lo (restituisca|ridia|renda)

traps.why: *Purché / a patto che* → subjunctive: *restituisca / ridia / renda*.
'As long as' here is a condition (*purché*), not duration (*finché*).

exercises.en: I'll lend you the book as long as you give it back to me.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: He left without anyone noticing.
answers: (Se n'è andato|È uscito|È andato via) senza che nessuno se ne accorgesse

traps.why: Past main verb → imperfetto: *se ne accorgesse*.

exercises.explanation: Different subjects + past → *senza che* + imperfetto: **se ne accorgesse**.
exercises.en: He left without anyone noticing.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: I'm telling you so that you know.

traps.why: *Perché tu sai* means 'because you know'. For 'so that', use the subjunctive: *perché tu lo sappia*.
*Così* + indicative is colloquial. Use *perché / affinché* + subjunctive for purpose.

exercises.en: I'm telling you so that you know.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: I'm going out, unless it rains.
answers: Esco a meno che non piova
exercises.explanation: *A meno che non* + subjunctive. The *non* is expletive: it doesn't negate.

exercises.instruction: Write 40–80 words in Italian.
exercises.prompt: A friend wants to borrow your flat for a weekend. Write a message setting your conditions. Use at least three different conjunctions from: purché, a patto che, a condizione che, a meno che, affinché, prima che, senza che, benché.

rubric.label: Uses at least three subjunctive conjunctions
rubric.hint: Try *purché tu…*, *a meno che non…*, *prima che…*

rubric.label: Uses present subjunctive forms
rubric.hint: After these conjunctions the verb goes into the subjunctive: *purché tu lasci…*

exercises.model: Ciao Luca! Ti lascio volentieri l'appartamento, purché tu lo lasci in ordine e non faccia feste. Ti do le chiavi venerdì, a meno che non arrivi troppo tardi. Prima che tu parta, ricordati di chiudere il gas e di innaffiare le piante, affinché non muoiano. E benché il vicino sia simpatico, non dargli le chiavi! Buon weekend!
exercises.explanation: Concessive, conditional, temporal and final conjunctions all take the subjunctive.

concepts.title: Subjunctive in relative clauses and after superlatives
concepts.rule: A relative clause takes the subjunctive when its antecedent is wanted but not identified (cerco qualcuno che sappia…), non-existent (non c'è nessuno che possa…), or follows a superlative, l'unico, il solo, il primo / l'ultimo (il più bello che abbia mai visto). A real, specific antecedent takes the indicative (ho trovato qualcuno che sa…).
assessment: Uses the subjunctive in relative clauses describing something sought, required or non-existent
Uses the indicative when the antecedent is a specific, existing person or thing
Uses the subjunctive after superlatives and l'unico / il solo in careful Italian
Applies the sequence of tenses inside relative clauses (cercavo qualcuno che potesse…)

lesson.intro: Here the subjunctive carries meaning on its own. *Cerco una segretaria che parla tedesco* suggests you have a particular person in mind; *che parli tedesco* means anyone with that skill will do. English can't show this difference with the verb, so English speakers default to the indicative. Using the subjunctive here, and after superlatives, is a hallmark of educated written Italian.

rules.title: Sought or required: subjunctive
rules.text: After *cercare, volere, avere bisogno di, servire*, when the antecedent is a type (any X that…) rather than a known individual, the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.it: Cerco un appartamento che **abbia** il terrazzo.
examples.en: I'm looking for a flat that has a terrace (any flat).

examples.it: Ho trovato un appartamento che **ha** il terrazzo.
examples.en: I've found a flat that has a terrace (a real one).

rules.title: Non-existent or doubtful: subjunctive
rules.text: After *non c'è nessuno / niente che*, *non conosco nessuno che*, *non esiste… che*, and in questions that doubt existence (*c'è qualcuno che… ?*), the relative clause takes the subjunctive.

examples.it: Non c'è niente che tu **possa** fare.
examples.en: There's nothing you can do.

examples.it: Non conosco nessuno che **sia** mai stato in Islanda.
examples.en: I don't know anyone who has ever been to Iceland.

rules.title: Superlatives, l'unico, il solo, il primo, l'ultimo
rules.text: After a relative superlative, and after *l'unico, il solo, il primo, l'ultimo* + *che*, careful Italian uses the subjunctive. In speech you'll often hear the indicative (*il più bello che ho visto*), but in writing and formal speech the subjunctive is expected.

examples.it: È il libro più bello che **abbia** mai **letto**.
examples.en: It's the best book I've ever read.
You're the only person who understands me.

rules.title: Not every 'il primo… che'
rules.text: *È la prima volta che…* introduces a real event, and it takes the **indicative**: *È la prima volta che **vengo** in Sicilia*. The same goes for any relative clause about something definite: *Il ragazzo che **abita** qui è mio cugino.*

rules.title: Sequence of tenses
rules.text: If the main verb is past or conditional, the relative clause moves to the imperfetto or trapassato.

head: Main verb present
Main verb past
rows: Non c'è nessuno che l'**abbia visto**.
Non c'era nessuno che l'**avesse visto**.

mistakes.wrong: Cerco una baby-sitter che parla inglese.
mistakes.right: Cerco una baby-sitter che parli inglese.
mistakes.why: You haven't found her yet: any babysitter with that skill → subjunctive.

mistakes.wrong: Ho una baby-sitter che parli inglese.
mistakes.right: Ho una baby-sitter che parla inglese.
mistakes.why: She exists and is specific → indicative.

mistakes.wrong: Non c'è niente che puoi fare.
mistakes.right: Non c'è niente che tu possa fare.
mistakes.why: Non-existent antecedent → subjunctive.

mistakes.wrong: Cercavo una casa che abbia il giardino.
mistakes.right: Cercavo una casa che avesse il giardino.
mistakes.why: Past main verb → imperfetto.

mistakes.wrong: È la prima volta che venga qui.
mistakes.right: È la prima volta che vengo qui.
mistakes.why: *È la prima volta che* describes a real event: indicative.

tips: Ask yourself: does this person or thing definitely exist and do I have one in mind? Yes → indicative. No, or 'any one that…' → subjunctive.
*Mai* after a superlative is a strong signal: *il più… che abbia mai…*.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Cerco una persona che ___ (sapere) usare Photoshop.

traps.why: You're looking for any person with that skill, not a specific one: subjunctive *sappia*.

exercises.en: I'm looking for someone who knows how to use Photoshop.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Non c'è nessuno che ___ (potere) aiutarmi.

traps.why: *Non c'è nessuno che* → the person doesn't exist: subjunctive *possa*.

exercises.en: There's nobody who can help me.

exercises.instruction: Complete in careful written Italian.
exercises.prompt: È il film più bello che ___ (vedere) quest'anno.

traps.why: In speech you'll hear *che ho visto*, but after a superlative careful Italian uses the subjunctive: *abbia visto*.
The seeing is in the past: congiuntivo passato *abbia visto*.

exercises.en: It's the best film I've seen this year.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Finalmente ho trovato un appartamento che ___ (avere) due terrazzi.

traps.why: You've found it: it's real and specific, so use the indicative *ha*.

exercises.en: I've finally found a flat that has two terraces.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Abbiamo bisogno di un medico che ___ (parlare) inglese.

traps.why: Any doctor who speaks English: required quality → subjunctive *parli*.

exercises.en: We need a doctor who speaks English.

exercises.instruction: Complete in careful written Italian.
exercises.prompt: Sei l'unica persona che mi ___ (capire) davvero.

traps.why: Common in speech, but after *l'unico / l'unica… che* careful Italian uses the subjunctive: *capisca*.

exercises.en: You're the only person who really understands me.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: L'agenzia cercava un traduttore che ___ (conoscere) bene il russo.

traps.why: Any translator with that skill → subjunctive. The indicative would mean a specific person they had in mind.

exercises.en: The agency was looking for a translator who knew Russian well.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Non conosco nessuno che ___ (essere) mai stato in Antartide.

traps.why: *Non conosco nessuno che* → no such person: subjunctive *sia (stato)*.
The main verb is present: *sia stato*.

exercises.en: I don't know anyone who has ever been to Antarctica.

exercises.instruction: Indicative or subjunctive? Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Conosco una ragazza che ___ (essere) stata in Antartide due volte.

traps.why: This girl exists and you know her: indicative *è stata*.

exercises.en: I know a girl who has been to Antarctica twice.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Ho un mal di testa terribile: dammi qualcosa che me lo ___ (fare) passare.

traps.why: Anything that will do the job, not a specific remedy: subjunctive *faccia*.
The main verb is an imperative (present): *faccia*.

exercises.en: I've got a terrible headache: give me something that'll make it go away.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Voglio una macchina che non ___ troppo.

optionWhy.0: You don't have this car yet: it's a requirement → subjunctive.
optionWhy.2: The main verb is present: present subjunctive.
optionWhy.3: No future here: a requirement takes the subjunctive.

exercises.en: I want a car that doesn't use too much fuel.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: È la prima volta che ___ in Sicilia.

optionWhy.1: *È la prima volta che* describes a real event that's happening: indicative.
optionWhy.2: No subjunctive here: it's a fact.
optionWhy.3: It's a fact happening now: indicative *vengo*.

traps.why: *È la prima volta che* + indicative: it reports a real event.

exercises.explanation: Trap: *è la prima volta che* reports a real event, so it takes the **indicative**, unlike *l'unico / il primo… che* used in a superlative sense.
exercises.en: It's the first time I've been to Sicily.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite starting with 'Cerco una collega che…' (you haven't found one yet).
exercises.prompt: Ho una collega che parla cinese.
answers: Cerco una collega che parli [il] cinese

traps.why: Now the colleague is only sought: subjunctive *parli*.

exercises.en: I'm looking for a colleague who speaks Chinese.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence into the past, starting with 'Cercavo…'.
exercises.prompt: Cerco qualcuno che possa aiutarmi.
answers: Cercavo qualcuno che (potesse aiutarmi|mi potesse aiutare)
exercises.en: I was looking for someone who could help me.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian, starting with 'Non c'è…' (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: There's nothing you can do.
exercises.en: There's nothing you can do.

exercises.instruction: Translate into careful written Italian.
exercises.prompt: She is the most intelligent person I know.
answers: [Lei] è la persona più intelligente che [io] conosca

traps.why: Colloquially *che conosco* is common, but after a superlative the written norm is the subjunctive: *conosca*.
That's the absolute superlative ('very intelligent'). Here you need the relative superlative: *la persona più intelligente che…*

exercises.en: She is the most intelligent person I know.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: I'm looking for a flat that has a garden and doesn't cost too much.
answers: (Cerco|Sto cercando) un (appartamento|alloggio) che abbia (un giardino|il giardino|giardino) e [che] non costi troppo

traps.why: Any flat with those features → subjunctive in both verbs: *abbia… costi*.
A flat (home) is *appartamento*. *Piatto* is a dish or 'flat' as an adjective.

exercises.en: I'm looking for a flat that has a garden and doesn't cost too much.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: It's the most beautiful book I've ever read.
answers: È il libro più bello che abbia mai letto
exercises.explanation: Superlative + *che* + congiuntivo passato, with *mai* between auxiliary and participle.

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian.
exercises.prompt: You run a small business and call a job agency. Say you're looking for someone who can start immediately.
answers: (Cerco|Cerchiamo|Sto cercando|Stiamo cercando) qualcuno che possa (cominciare|iniziare) subito

traps.why: You don't have this person yet: subjunctive *possa*.

exercises.en: I'm looking for someone who can start immediately.

concepts.title: Indefinites (chiunque, qualunque…) and the independent subjunctive
concepts.rule: Chiunque, qualunque / qualsiasi (+ noun), dovunque / ovunque and comunque introducing a clause take the subjunctive (Qualunque cosa tu faccia…). The subjunctive also stands alone in suppositions (Che sia già partito?), wishes (Magari fosse vero!) and exhortations (Sia chiaro…, Che entri!).
assessment: Uses the subjunctive after chiunque, qualunque / qualsiasi, dovunque and comunque introducing a clause
Keeps qualunque / qualsiasi singular and distinguishes comunque (= however + clause) from comunque (= anyway)
Uses Che + subjunctive for suppositions and Magari / Se solo + imperfetto for wishes
Distinguishes magari + subjunctive (if only) from magari + indicative (maybe)
Recognises and uses fixed exhortative formulas (Sia chiaro, Che entri pure, Viva…)

lesson.intro: 'Whoever', 'whatever', 'wherever' and 'however' all open subjunctive clauses in Italian. The subjunctive can also stand without any main verb, which is where much of its expressive power in C1 speech lies: *Che sia già partito?* (Could he have left already?), *Magari!* (If only!), *Sia chiaro* (Let it be clear). English uses modal verbs or *if only* here, so learners rarely produce these forms on their own.

rules.title: Chiunque, qualunque / qualsiasi, dovunque, comunque + subjunctive
rules.text: *Chiunque* (whoever), *qualunque / qualsiasi + noun* (whatever, whichever), *dovunque / ovunque* (wherever) and *comunque* (however, in whatever way) take the subjunctive. *Qualunque* and *qualsiasi* are invariable and singular: *qualunque **cosa***, not ~~qualunque cose~~.

examples.it: Chiunque **sia**, digli che non ci sono.
examples.en: Whoever it is, tell them I'm not in.
Whatever you decide, I'll back you.
Wherever he goes, he always finds friends.
However it goes, it'll be an experience.

rules.title: Contrast: when there's no subjunctive
rules.text: *Comunque* at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma, means 'anyway', a discourse marker with an ordinary indicative verb: *Comunque, domani **parto***. *Qualunque* / *qualsiasi* after a noun means 'ordinary': *un giorno qualunque*.

examples.en: Anyway, Marco's arriving tomorrow.
It was an ordinary Tuesday.

rules.title: Supposition: Che + subjunctive?
rules.text: A question starting with *Che* + subjunctive voices a worried or puzzled guess: 'Could it be that…?' Use the congiuntivo passato for past events. The future of supposition (*Sarà già partito?*) is a common alternative.

examples.en: He's not answering. Could he be ill?
Could she have forgotten the appointment?

rules.title: Wishes: Magari / Se solo / Almeno + imperfetto or trapassato
rules.text: For unlikely or impossible wishes use the **imperfetto** (present) or **trapassato** (past): *Magari fosse vero!* *Se solo l'avessi saputo!* The subjunctive can even stand alone: *Potessi partire anch'io!* Careful: *magari* + **indicative** means 'maybe': *Magari viene anche Luca* (Maybe Luca's coming too).

examples.en: If only we won the lottery!
If only you'd listened to your mother!

rules.title: Exhortations and formulas
rules.text: The present subjunctive gives third-person commands and set formulas: *Sia chiaro* (let it be clear), *Che entri pure* (let him come in), *Viva gli sposi!*, *Dio ce la mandi buona*. The formal *Lei* imperative is in fact a subjunctive: *Si accomodi, Mi dica*.

mistakes.wrong: Chiunque è, non apro.
mistakes.why: *Chiunque* introducing a clause → subjunctive.

mistakes.wrong: Qualunque cose tu faccia…
mistakes.why: *Qualunque / qualsiasi* are singular only.

mistakes.wrong: Magari è vero!
mistakes.why: A wish needs *magari* + imperfetto. *Magari è vero* means 'maybe it's true'.

mistakes.wrong: Dovunque vai, ti seguo.
mistakes.why: *Dovunque* → subjunctive.

mistakes.wrong: Che è già partito?
mistakes.why: A *Che…?* supposition needs the subjunctive.

tips: *Comunque vada* is a fixed phrase worth memorising: 'however it turns out'.
For a hopeful-but-realistic wish, *speriamo che* + present subjunctive is often better than *magari*: *Speriamo che non piova!*
Signal for the wish meaning: an exclamation mark and the imperfetto. Signal for 'maybe': the indicative.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Chiunque ___ (essere), digli che non ci sono.
exercises.en: Whoever it is, tell them I'm not in.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Qualunque cosa tu ___ (decidere), io ti appoggerò.

traps.why: Use the present subjunctive, not the future, after *qualunque cosa*.

exercises.en: Whatever you decide, I'll back you.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Dovunque tu ___ (andare), ti verrò a cercare.
exercises.en: Wherever you go, I'll come looking for you.

exercises.instruction: Complete the wish with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Magari ___ (essere) vero!

traps.why: *Magari è vero* means 'maybe it's true'. For the wish 'If only it were true!' use *magari fosse*.

exercises.en: If only it were true!

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Comunque ___ (andare) a finire, io non mi pento di niente.
exercises.en: However it ends up, I don't regret anything.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Sono le dieci e Paolo non è ancora arrivato. Che ___ (perdere) il treno?

traps.why: A *Che…?* supposition needs the subjunctive: *abbia perso*.
Missing the train would already have happened: congiuntivo passato.
Without *Che*, *Avrà perso il treno?* (future of supposition) would be fine. After *Che*, the target is *abbia perso*.

exercises.explanation: Independent supposition about the past → *Che* + **abbia perso**?
exercises.en: It's ten o'clock and Paolo still hasn't arrived. Could he have missed the train?

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Qualsiasi decisione ___ (prendere) il consiglio, la rispetteremo.
exercises.en: Whatever decision the council takes, we'll respect it.

exercises.instruction: Careful: here *magari* means 'maybe'. Complete with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Magari ___ (venire) anche Luca stasera, non lo so ancora.

traps.why: *Magari* = 'maybe' takes the indicative. Only *magari* = 'if only' (a wish) takes the subjunctive.

exercises.en: Maybe Luca's coming tonight too, I don't know yet.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Chiunque ___ (vedere) qualcosa ieri sera è pregato di contattare la polizia.

traps.why: *Ieri sera* is past: congiuntivo passato *abbia visto*.

exercises.en: Anyone who saw anything last night is asked to contact the police.

exercises.instruction: Complete the exhortation with the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Il signor Neri è arrivato? Che ___ (entrare) pure!

traps.why: Third-person command (*let him come in*): *Che* + present subjunctive *entri*.

exercises.en: Has Mr Neri arrived? Let him come in!

exercises.instruction: Choose the fixed formula meaning 'Let it be clear'.
exercises.prompt: ___ chiaro: non tollererò altri ritardi.

optionWhy.1: *È chiaro* states that something is clear. The warning formula 'let it be clear' is *Sia chiaro*.
optionWhy.2: *Fosse chiaro* would be a wish ('if only it were clear').

exercises.explanation: Exhortative subjunctive in a fixed formula: **Sia chiaro**.
exercises.en: Let it be clear: I won't tolerate any more delays.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form.
exercises.prompt: Qualunque ___ i tuoi motivi, non puoi comportarti così.

optionWhy.3: The main verb is present: present subjunctive.

traps.why: The verb agrees with *i tuoi motivi*: *siano*.

exercises.en: Whatever your reasons are, you can't behave like this.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form. Watch the comma.
exercises.prompt: Comunque, Marco ___ domani: ne parliamo con lui.

optionWhy.1: *Comunque,* with a comma = 'anyway', a discourse marker. It doesn't introduce a subjunctive clause.
optionWhy.2: Not a wish or hypothesis: indicative.

exercises.en: Anyway, Marco's arriving tomorrow: we'll talk to him about it.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite as a wish starting with 'Magari…'.
exercises.prompt: Vorrei avere più tempo.

traps.why: *Magari ho più tempo* means 'maybe I'll have more time'. For a wish: *magari avessi*.

exercises.en: If only I had more time!

exercises.instruction: Rewrite as a supposition starting with 'Che…?'.
exercises.prompt: Forse si è dimenticato dell'appuntamento.
exercises.en: Could he have forgotten the appointment?

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian (informal 'you').
exercises.prompt: Whatever you do, don't tell her.
exercises.en: Whatever you do, don't tell her.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian.
exercises.prompt: If only it were true!

traps.why: A wish needs the imperfect subjunctive: *fosse*.

exercises.en: If only it were true!

exercises.instruction: Translate into Italian using 'Che…?'.
exercises.prompt: Could he have already left?
answers: Che (sia già partito|se ne sia già andato|sia già andato via)

traps.why: Correct Italian (future of supposition). The task asked for *Che* + subjunctive: *Che sia già partito?*
*Potrebbe essere partito* is possible, but the task asks for the independent subjunctive: *Che sia già partito?*

exercises.explanation: Independent supposition about the past → *Che* + congiuntivo passato.
exercises.en: Could he have already left?

exercises.instruction: Put the words in order.
exercises.prompt: Wherever you go, I'll follow you.
exercises.explanation: *Dovunque* + subjunctive clause, then the main clause (or the other way round).

exercises.instruction: Say it in Italian (informal).
exercises.prompt: Someone is knocking at the door while you're on the phone. Tell your flatmate: whoever it is, tell them I'm not here.
answers: Chiunque sia (digli|dille|di') che non ci sono
exercises.en: Whoever it is, tell them I'm not here.
